parts.text: Suggest two causes of lack of sharpness of an X-ray image.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The thickness of a sheet of metal is examined using a parallel X-ray beam, as illustrated in Fig. 12.1.

{{figure:figure_12_1.png}}

Part of the beam passes normally through the metal of thickness $3.2\text{ mm}$. Another part of the beam passes normally through the metal of thickness $x\text{ mm}$.

The linear attenuation (absorption) coefficient for the X-ray beam in the metal is $1.5\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

The ratio

$$\frac{\text{intensity of X-ray beam transmitted through 3.2 mm of metal}}{\text{intensity of X-ray beam transmitted through }x\text{ mm of metal}}$$

is found to be 0.81.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: The ratio of the intensities is also the ratio of the powers of the X-ray beams. Calculate this ratio in decibels.
